name: verilog_compiler
content: The code has no compile error. I should give this implementation to the user.

**The bug:** The erroneous implementation used a sequential (clocked) always block — `always @(posedge clk)` — but the module has no `clk` input, so the simulator cannot bind `clk`, causing the elaboration errors. A 2-to-1 mux is purely combinational logic and must not be clocked.

**The fix:** Replace the clocked always block with a combinational always block (`always @(*)`) using blocking assignments (or equivalently a continuous `assign` statement).

```verilog
module top_module (
	input sel,
	input [7:0] a,
	input [7:0] b,
	output reg [7:0] out
);

	always @(*) begin
		out = (~sel & a) | (sel & b);
	end

endmodule
```

This compiles cleanly and implements the required 8-bit 2-to-1 mux: `out = a` when `sel = 0`, and `out = b` when `sel = 1`.
